cards.text: Time to head south to Judah, friend. In the fourth year of Ahab's reign over Israel, Jehoshaphat son of Asa becomes king of Judah. Jeho-SHA-phat. Say it with me. It sounds like a sneeze wearing a crown.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat is thirty-five years old when he becomes king. How long does he reign in Jerusalem?

cards.text: His mother's name is Azubah daughter of Shilhi. Now the big question for every king in this book: what kind of king is he gonna be?

cards.question: When it comes to how he lives, whose ways does Jehoshaphat walk in?
Jehoshaphat doesn't turn away from his father's ways. He does what is ___ in the eyes of the LORD.

cards.text: A GOOD king! Papa's doing a happy dance right here on his gold base! But hold on, friend. This book loves a "however," and here it comes.

cards.question: Something in Judah doesn't get removed during Jehoshaphat's reign. What is it?
Once Jehoshaphat is king, the people stop sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.

cards.text: Next up: Jehoshaphat and his neighbor to the north, the king of Israel. Every king's got a neighbor like that. The one you wave at from the driveway and hope doesn't walk over.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat goes to war against the king of Israel.

cards.text: The rest of his acts, his might and how he waged war, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah. But this book still makes room for one more cleanup job.

cards.question: Some people were still in the land from the days of Jehoshaphat's father Asa. Who does Jehoshaphat banish?

cards.text: Over in Edom, there's no king, just a deputy serving as king. Meanwhile, Jehoshaphat builds ships of Tarshish to sail to Ophir.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat's ships of Tarshish are headed to Ophir for ___.
Big ships, big plans, a trip to Ophir for gold. What happens to Jehoshaphat's ships?

answers.text: They're wrecked before they ever sail
They come home loaded with gold
Edom captures them out at sea

cards.text: Wrecked at Ezion-geber. Never even left. I KNOW that feeling, friend: you mix the dough, preheat the oven, and the whole tray slides off the counter before it ever sees the heat.
At that time, Ahaziah son of Ahab says to Jehoshaphat, “Let my servants sail with your servants,” and waits on an answer.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat agrees to let Ahaziah's servants sail with his servants.

cards.text: He says no. Then Jehoshaphat rests with his fathers and is buried with them in the city of his father David.

cards.question: Who reigns in Jehoshaphat's place in Judah?

cards.text: Now back up north. In the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's reign over Judah, Ahaziah son of Ahab becomes king of Israel in Samaria.

cards.question: How long does Ahaziah reign in Samaria?
Like Jehoshaphat, Ahaziah does what is right in the sight of the LORD.
Ahaziah walks in the ways of his father and mother, and in the ways of one more man, the one who caused Israel to sin. Who?
Ahaziah serves and worships ___, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger.

cards.text: Just as his father had done. Following in your father's footsteps only works, friend, if those footsteps were headed somewhere good.

findings.problem: The opening card has five sentences: "Time to head south to Judah, friend." / "In the fourth year..." / "Jeho-SHA-phat." / "Say it with me." / "It sounds like a sneeze wearing a crown." The limit is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The joke makes fun of Jehoshaphat's name itself ("sounds like a sneeze wearing a crown"). That laughs at the person in the Bible story, not with his human situation.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The core action in verse 44 is making peace with the king of Israel. The comparison is about avoiding a neighbor you hope stays away, which is the opposite action. It also hints at a distance or tension the text never gives.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Verse 44's actual detail, that Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel, is never told. This true/false card only teaches that he didn't go to war against him, and no story card states the peace. The baker leaves without that detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "Meanwhile" ties the deputy king in Edom (v47) and Jehoshaphat building ships (v48) together as happening at the same time. The text doesn't say how these two things connect, and it gives no time link between them.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
